extracted.intended_audience: petitioners, regulated industry, legal counsel, public commenters, FDA staff, and media seeking to participate in or understand FDA administrative proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and procedural rules governing FDA administrative practices: submission of documents and petitions to the Dockets Management Staff, initiation and conduct of administrative proceedings, public disclosure rules, good guidance practices, and policies/procedures for electronic media coverage of public administrative proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Part 10
rubrics_metrics.description: Part 10 governs practices and procedures for petitions, hearings, and other administrative proceedings and activities conducted by the Food and Drug Administration under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, the Public Health Service Act, and other laws which the Commissioner of Food and Drugs administers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a requirement in another part of title 21 differs from a requirement in this part, the requirements of this part apply to the extent they do not conflict. References to 'publication' or 'to publish' refer to publication in the Federal Register unless otherwise noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions and use of defined terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms used throughout the part (e.g., Act, administrative action, administrative file, administrative record, Dockets Management Staff, ex parte communication, interested person, meeting, participant, petitioner, petition, presiding officer, proceeding, public advisory committee, order, regulatory hearing) have specific meanings for purposes of Part 10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A term defined in section 201 of the FD&C Act or part 1 has the same meaning here. Words in singular include plural and masculine include feminine. References to persons in FDA include delegates. The definition of 'ex parte communication' clarifies it is an off-the-record communication for which reasonable prior notice to all parties is not given, but excludes status report requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summaries of administrative practices and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner will prepare for public distribution summaries of FDA administrative practices and procedures in readily understandable terms to encourage public participation in all agency activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These summaries are intended to increase accessibility and public understanding of agency administrative processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver, suspension, or modification of procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner or a presiding officer may waive, suspend, or modify any provision in parts 12 through 16 applicable to the conduct of a public hearing if no participant will be prejudiced, the ends of justice will be served, and the action is in accordance with law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver may be voluntary or at the request of a participant and may be announced at the hearing or by notice in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission to Dockets Management Staff — copies, signature, and filing location
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission to the Dockets Management Staff of a petition, comment, objection, notice, compilation of information, or any other document is to be filed in four copies except as otherwise provided. Submissions must be signed by the person making it or an attorney/authorized representative and mailed or delivered to the Dockets Management Staff address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trade association submissions are also subject to §10.105(b). Electronically submitted petitions may follow different copy rules as specified elsewhere. Filings are subject to technical review by the Dockets Management Staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission content — include full information; no incorporation by reference unless previously submitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Information referred to or relied upon in a submission is to be included in full and may not be incorporated by reference, unless previously submitted in the same proceeding. A copy of an article or other reference cited must be included except for reported Federal court cases, Federal laws/regulations, routinely available FDA documents, or recognized medical/scientific textbooks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only part of a submitted document is relevant, delete irrelevant information and submit only the relevant portion. Failure to include full supporting material can lead to rejection or exclusion from consideration of the noncomplying portion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign language submissions — translation and verification
rubrics_metrics.description: If part of the material submitted is in a foreign language, it must be accompanied by an English translation verified to be complete and accurate, plus the translator's name, address, and a brief statement of qualifications. The translation must be accompanied by copies of the original publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translations must be reliable and accompanied by the original-language materials to permit agency review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redaction requirements — personal identifiers and defamatory material
rubrics_metrics.description: Names and other information that would identify patients or research subjects must be deleted to preclude a clearly unwarranted invasion of personal privacy. Defamatory, scurrilous, or intemperate matter must be deleted before submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure submissions do not include personally identifying data or offensive material; otherwise portions may be excluded from consideration or returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of deficient submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to comply with the requirements of this part or with §12.80 or §13.20 will result in rejection of the submission for filing or, if filed, exclusion from consideration of any portion that fails to comply. The Dockets Management Staff will not file submissions with known deficiencies but will return them with a copy of applicable regulations indicating noncompliance. A deficient submission may be corrected or supplemented and subsequently filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Dockets Management Staff does not make confidentiality decisions; correcting deficiencies promptly can allow re-filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing does not imply merits; filing date and computation of time
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing of a submission means only that the Dockets Management Staff has identified no technical deficiencies; it does not imply that it meets all requirements or that it contains reasonable grounds for the requested action. Except as provided in §10.31(b), submissions are considered submitted on the date postmarked or the date delivered in person during regular business hours; some regulations require received-by dates and will treat submission as of the date received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Saturdays, Sundays, and Federal legal holidays are included in computing time, but if a deadline falls on such a day it extends to the next business day. Be mindful of statutes or specific sections that require receipt rather than postmark.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature, representations, and legal exposure
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission must be signed by the person making it or an authorized representative. All submissions are representations that, to the best of the submitter's knowledge, information, and belief, the statements made are true and accurate and are subject to the False Reports to the Government Act (18 U.S.C. 1001).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Willfully false statements in submissions can be criminal offenses; ensure veracity and proper authorization for signing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment of receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA ordinarily will not acknowledge or give receipt for documents except for documents delivered in person or by certified/registered mail with return receipt requested, and petitions for which acknowledgment of receipt of filing is provided by regulation or customary practice (e.g., §10.30(c) citizen petitions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use certified/registered mail or in-person delivery if an acknowledgment of receipt is required or desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of submissions and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in paragraphs (j)(2) and (3), certain submissions (e.g., petitions, comments on petitions/documents published in the Federal Register, objections/requests for hearings, material submitted at hearings, and material placed on public display such as guidance documents) will be on public display and available for public examination during normal business hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for copies are handled under subpart C of part 20. Material identified by §20.63 as a clearly unwarranted invasion of personal privacy or material of the types listed in §10.20(j)(2)(i) will not be on public display unless otherwise applicable or disclosed under a protective order. Material to be withheld must be segregated and clearly marked; disagreements about withholding can be raised to the Associate Commissioner for Public Affairs for a ruling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of material ordinarily not publicly disclosed
rubrics_metrics.description: Material not on public display includes safety and effectiveness information (animal/human studies; tests for identity, stability, purity, potency, bioavailability, performance, usefulness), protocols for tests/studies, manufacturing methods/processes including quality control, production/sales/distribution information (with limited aggregated exceptions), quantitative/semiquantitative formulas, and product design or construction information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such material must be segregated and marked; in hearings it may be disclosed under protective order and only in camera to those specified by the judge or presiding officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiation of administrative proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: An administrative proceeding may be initiated (a) by an interested person petitioning the Commissioner (in prescribed forms), (b) by the Commissioner initiating a proceeding where FDA has primary jurisdiction or concludes administrative determination is appropriate, or (c) when a court refers or holds a matter in abeyance and the Commissioner deems an administrative determination feasible within agency priorities/resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commissioner may use procedures in this part to review matters initiated under paragraph (b) and may utilize conferences, hearings, Federal Register notices, proposals, or other public procedures in reviewing petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizen petition format and required content
rubrics_metrics.description: A citizen petition must be submitted in accordance with §10.20 and (if applicable) §10.31 and must follow the specified format: Date, Statement of statutory authority, Action Requested (exact wording of existing and proposed regulation/order or specific relief requested), Statement of Grounds (full, well-organized factual and legal grounds including unfavorable information), Environmental Impact (categorical exclusion claim or environmental assessment), Economic Impact (when requested by Commissioner), and Certification that the petition includes all information and views relied upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions may be submitted electronically via Regulations.gov or by mail. Confidential petitions require submission of original and redacted copies. A petition that appears to meet form requirements will be filed, stamped with filing date, and assigned a unique docket number; subsequent submissions must reference that docket number. Comments on a filed petition specifying the docket number become part of the docket file. A request for alternative administrative action must be a separate petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner response timelines and possible dispositions for petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner shall, considering agency resources, priority, and statutory time requirements, rule upon each filed petition and generally furnish a response within 180 days. The response may approve, deny, dismiss (if moot), or provide a tentative response indicating inability to reach decision. Special timelines: respond within 90 days for petitions filed under section 505(j)(2)(C); the Commissioner intends to respond within 150 days for petitions subject to section 505(q).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses implementing approvals will trigger appropriate actions (e.g., Federal Register notice). The Commissioner may grant or deny petitions in whole or part and may take other relief as warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementing, amending, withdrawing petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner may supplement, amend, or withdraw a petition without agency approval and without prejudice until the Commissioner rules, unless the petition has been referred for a hearing under parts 12–15. After ruling or referral, supplementation, amendment, or withdrawal requires Commissioner approval; withdrawal may be approved with or without prejudice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely amendments before referral are permitted; after referral obtain Commissioner approval to avoid procedural issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative record composition and exclusivity
rubrics_metrics.description: The administrative record for a petition includes the petition and all information it relies on, all comments received, documents specified in §10.40(g) if the petition resulted in a proposal, transcripts/minutes/reports/Federal Register notices from optional procedures, the Commissioner's decision and supporting information, documents filed under §10.65(h), and records for petitions for reconsideration or stay where applicable. The administrative record is the exclusive record for the Commissioner's decision and closes on the date of decision unless otherwise specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information not in the administrative record cannot be used to challenge the Commissioner's decision; persons wishing to rely on new information must submit a new petition to modify the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizen petitions related to ANDAs, certain NDAs, or certain BLAs — certification and verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Special rules apply to petitions that could delay approval of an ANDA (section 505(j)), certain 505(b)(2) NDAs, or 351(k) BLAs submitted on/after Sept 27, 2007: such petitions are regarded as submitted on receipt; FDA will not consider a petition unless it is in writing and contains a specified certification (including specific dates and identification of information categories); supplemental information/comments are not accepted unless they are in writing and contain a specified verification with dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict certification/verification and timing rules apply to petitions that could impact abbreviated/new drug application or biosimilar approvals; failure to include required certifications/verification will result in non-consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative reconsideration of action
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may reconsider a matter on the Commissioner's own initiative or on petition of an interested person. A request for reconsideration of all or part of a Commissioner decision on a petition must be submitted in accordance with §10.20 and in the prescribed form no later than 30 days after the date of decision (Commissioner may permit later filing for good cause).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a decision is published in the Federal Register, the day of publication is the day of decision. Reconsideration petitions must follow the required format and deadlines to be considered timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of openness for electronic media coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA presumes agency public administrative proceedings are open to electronic media coverage and will permit, whenever possible, interested persons to record such proceedings subject to procedures and limited restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guideline clarifies policy to facilitate media access and notes that videotape recordings are not the official record (the official record is the written transcript). The presiding officer retains discretionary authority to regulate the conduct of proceedings to ensure fairness and timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures and restrictions for electronic media coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons intending to record should provide advance notice (preferably 48 hours) to the Press Relations Staff with details on duration, equipment, and special needs. Equipment should be stationary and set up before proceedings or during breaks; roving cameras are not permitted; off-the-record portions may not be videotaped. When space is limited, presiding officers may limit number of cameras and require pool arrangements. Additional conditions may be imposed only under exceptional circumstances where electronic recording would cause disruption, prejudice fairness, or impair witness testimony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presiding officers may issue written additional conditions; appeals of additional requirements may be made to the Deputy Commissioner or Associate Commissioner for Regulatory Affairs and do not require interruption of proceedings. If additional restrictions are imposed during a hearing, the presiding officer must notify senior officials and provide a written explanation promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good Guidance Practices (GGP) — development, availability, and non-binding nature
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA follows Good Guidance Practices for guidance documents: guidance documents are the agency's current thinking and do not create or confer rights and are not binding. FDA will make guidance documents available in hard copy and electronically, maintain a current internet list of guidance documents (adding new documents within 30 days of issuance), and publish a comprehensive list annually in the Federal Register identifying added/withdrawn documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If someone believes FDA staff treated guidance as binding or failed to follow GGPs, they should first contact the relevant supervisor or ombudsman and may escalate to the Office of the Chief Mediator and Ombudsman. Guidance development and issuance procedures, including opportunities to seek clarification or challenge the use of guidance as binding, are described in the GGP section.
